page: Amazon Web Services m4.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Xen hypervisor and an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor. Running on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB per core, and a 45 MB L3 cache. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the m4.xlarge in the lower performance tiers. Single-core and multi-core CPU stress-ng tests register in the bottom 25 percent, with scores of 1282.39 and 3353.46 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests also reflect legacy hardware constraints, showing 24.01 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 21.65 GB/sec for large block write operations. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Redis SET operations fall into the bottom 10 percent of tested instances, with Redis processing 1.44 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m4.xlarge offers a balanced resource allocation profile but operates on older-generation hardware, resulting in lower performance per resource compared to newer instance families. It is best suited for legacy general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, development environments, and lightweight background tasks that do not require high computational throughput, fast local storage, or high-speed networking.
